analysis:
Reviewed StartupPreloadTests.swift, a test-only file. The base_text excerpt (lines 654-1146) and head_text (lines 1-650) were examined. The visible diff adds a PreloadRecorder event log (_events, recordWarmup) and a shapeWarmup dependency in the makeDeps test helper. New test shapeWarmupFollowsPassingSelfTests (head lines ~313-330) and shapeWarmupFollowsLoadWithoutSelfTest (~332-342) assert that the warmup runs after each passing self-test, runs before the next load, is skipped for failed loads or self-tests, and still runs for fail-open self-test failures only when the self-test passes. Changed head ranges 311-341 are covered.

The file contains no production code, no auth, crypto, network or key handling, and no changes to the coordinator contract. Temp files are written under the temporary directory with UUID names. Fake HF snapshots are created in the real HF cache dir (makeFakeHFSnapshot) and cleaned up with defer. This is pre-existing test hygiene and not a security issue.

Relevant threat IDs: T-028 and T-041 involve residual KV data and the prefix cache, and T-029 involves availability. A shape-warmup step on a loaded model could touch GPU and KV state, but the warmup content is not visible in this test file. The production StartupPreloader and ProviderLoop warmup implementation is not in the supplied evidence. The next pass should check that the warmup uses synthetic non-consumer prompts. It should also confirm that it does not donate to the SSD prefix cache (T-041, SSDPrefixCache.donate) or publish performance estimates. The existing test startupSelfTestDoesNotPublishThroughput suggests the self-test avoids that. The patch excerpt is truncated, so changes between head lines 311-341 are only partly visible; the head_text unit ends at line 650.

No security regression is identified from the test changes alone.
